required_skills: Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Science
key_responsibilities: Develop embedded firmware for motor controllers and generator control electronics
Design and implement bare-metal C software on 32-bit microcontrollers
Create low-level drivers, hardware interfaces, and platform services
Support hardware bring-up, debugging, and system verification
Contribute to software architecture, interfaces, and coding standards
Write requirements, specifications, and test procedures
Support lab, environmental, EMI/EMC, and field testing

strengths: Bare-metal C on a 32-bit MCU is real, not a keyword: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor programs GPIO, TIM2, ADC1 and I2C1 directly at register level, with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and a hand-written low-level I2C driver in 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz rate.

Interrupt-driven design has first-principles depth: a 4-bit A/B quadrature transition state machine on hardware interrupts (Robocon, 2400 CPR encoders), plus interrupt-driven UART command handling with user override on the Object Tracking Turret.
Low-level driver authorship is demonstrated twice independently (I2C driver on STM32, quadrature decode on Arduino Due) rather than consuming vendor HAL libraries.

Motor drive at a hardware level: four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM via DuePWM, angle-weighted joystick-to-wheel mixing derived from atan2 to eliminate PWM saturation at 45 degree diagonals, and closed-loop heading correction feeding encoder-derived angular error back into rotation PWM.

Hardware bring-up is backed by fabrication, not just integration: custom single-layer PCBs designed in EAGLE and fabricated for locomotive robots, then brought up with UART and I2C sensor communication and closed-loop feedback.

Systematic hardware-adjacent debugging: 11 integration failures resolved on the COFFIN capstone including servo brown-out and stale-frame capture, and sensor jitter resolved through software calibration and resolution tuning at Planctech.
Safety reflex exists in the motor context: a fail-safe state machine that halts all motor channels on controller disconnect.
real_gaps: Generator control systems / genset controls — no exposure anywhere in the profile
Power electronics — no inverter, gate drive, current sensing, dead-time or bus-voltage work; all motor work goes through off-the-shelf Cytron driver modules
Field-oriented control and control-loop tuning on a real motor — no PID tuning, no current or velocity loop; closed-loop heading correction is the only feedback control evidence
TI C2000 / C28x toolchain and peripheral set (ePWM, ADC triggering, CLA) — zero
CAN bus — zero (the only 'CAN' string in the profile is CanSat)
JTAG / SWD hardware debugging on silicon — zero; the flagship bare-metal project was verified in Proteus simulation
Formal system verification — no requirements traceability, specifications, or written test procedures
EMI/EMC, environmental (thermal/vibration) and field testing — zero
MISRA C and DO-178C or any safety-critical software process
Platform-scale work: platform services layer, coding standards ownership, interface contracts across a firmware product line
Seniority (prose note, not scored): the JD expects 4+ years and independent module ownership from design through verification; profile is capstone, research and internship scope
overstated_by_keywords: 'Motor control' as HAVE — it is PWM generation into pre-built driver modules, not motor controller firmware; no commutation, no current loop, no FOC

'Embedded debugging and troubleshooting' as HAVE — oscilloscopes and logic analyzers are listed as tools but no bullet shows scope-based signal debugging; the evidence is integration and software-level debugging
'32-bit microcontrollers' as HAVE — true for STM32 Cortex-M4, but the motor and encoder work sits on Arduino Due under the Arduino framework, not bare-metal register access

'Software architecture' as ADJACENT — the architecture evidence (Frame Simulator module decoupling, COFFIN three-layer pipeline) is Python, desktop and distributed-systems architecture, not firmware platform architecture
understated_by_keywords: Hardware bring-up scored only ADJACENT, but designing, fabricating and then bringing up custom EAGLE PCBs with UART/I2C sensor comms is literal board bring-up
'Safety-critical software' scored flat MISSING, yet the fail-safe state machine halting all motors on controller disconnect is exactly the reasoning pattern a motor-controller interviewer probes for
'Interrupt-driven systems' as a single HAVE tag undersells writing quadrature decode from first principles as a 4-bit transition state machine on hardware interrupts
Resource-constrained determinism (3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, deterministic 1 Hz update) is a real firmware discipline the JD implies but never names, so the keyword pass never credited it
screening_gaps: 4+ years of professional embedded firmware experience against 0 full-time years — Actalent is a staffing agency billing a client, so years-in-seat is a contractual filter rather than a soft preference and is the single most likely rejection reason

No motor-controller or power-electronics domain evidence — the role's entire subject matter (motor controllers, generator control electronics, FOC) has no backing; off-the-shelf Cytron drivers on a competition robot will not read as motor control to this hiring manager
No TI C2000/C28x and no on-silicon debugger experience — JTAG is a stated required qualification, and the flagship bare-metal project was verified in Proteus simulation rather than on hardware
llm_analysis.reasoning: The required-qualification spine of this role is genuinely covered: bare-metal C at register level on a Cortex-M4, interrupt-driven design written from first principles, hand-authored low-level drivers, and real PWM motor drive with encoder feedback. What is missing is the entire subject matter — motor controller and generator control electronics, power electronics, FOC, TI C2000, CAN, MISRA/DO-178C, and formal verification and EMI/EMC testing — so the profile reads as a capable embedded generalist applying to a power-electronics firmware specialist req that wants 4+ years. The semantic read lands within a point of the keyword score, which is unusual and means the keyword pass was not inflating anything here; the honest read is that this specific requisition is a long shot, though the Actalent recruiter relationship has option value across their other embedded reqs.
